Meta.title: Passiona — AI literacy for primary schools
Meta.description: Two 20-lesson AI-literacy programmes for Primary 1 and Primary 5. Students build, test and explain AI through four connected creative tools.

Hero.title: Build AI. Question it. Shape what comes next.
Hero.subtitle: Two hands-on, 20-lesson journeys for Primary 1 and Primary 5. Students make AI visible, test ideas with evidence and build a connected world they can explain.
proof: No child accounts or personal data

goals: Want to teach AI literacy, but don't know where to start.
Want students to truly understand AI, not just use AI apps.
Want visible learning outcomes you can show.
Want to make the most of EDB funding.
help: Two complete journeys for Primary 1 and Primary 5, each using the AI Workshop, Fit Studio, Coding Buddy and AI City.
Students build, test and discuss AI ideas through hands-on tools and their own city.
Outcomes students can show: a city, a Champion and a project they can explain with evidence.
Funding guidance. We help you navigate and apply for EDB support.

workshop.title: Build AI abilities
workshop.hoverText: Assemble real AI machines in the Workshop.
points: Assemble, don't just use. Drag real pieces and wire them together to build working AI.
Real concepts, made visible. The machines learn, sort, and invent on their own.
See the machine think. Models train, test, and fail in real time. Watch why, not just what.

city.title: Connect & run
city.hoverText: Plug your machines into the world.
points: Your abilities become the world. Every Workshop machine plugs in as a capability building.
Explore the AI City where students place their machines, plan streets and test their ideas.
A living world in motion. Weather, citizens, and crises test every system.
Run what you built. The sorter you wired actually sorts the city's waste.

champion.kicker: Your AI Champion — made in Fit Studio
champion.title: Make it yours
champion.hoverText: Walk any scenario as the champion you built.
points: Design your own champion. Skins, colours, and gear: crowns, visors, jetpacks.
Walk through any scenario as your champion, in third person.
One identity everywhere. Your champion carries your abilities into every world.

build.title: Understand AI by building it
steps: Start from an example. Open a finished machine (recycle sorter, watchdog, bandit pet) and see a working model.
Wire it yourself. Connect the camera to the sorter, teach it what to look for, and watch the belt do the rest.
Make it yours. Rename the bins, add rules, invent a machine nobody has built before.

machines.title: Six starter machines, six AI ideas
machines.lead: Start from these six machines, then remix them. Rename the bins, add rules, and invent machines nobody has built before.

rows.idea: Image classification: a belt eye that guesses what you show it.
Anomaly detection: barks at anything not taught as “normal”.
Unsupervised learning: the machine invents its own piles.
Feedback learning: clap for the trick you like, it learns your favourite.
Train/test discipline: study some data, test the rest.
A readable rule drawn live: how many, not which one.

city.title: From the bench to the scene
steps: Build the ability in the Workshop. Your way, not a fixed answer.
Bring in your champion. Save it, then step into the scenario.
See it govern. The ability you built operates a live district, solving the scenario’s challenge.

sections.heading: Scope and our approach
paragraphs: This policy explains how Passiona handles personal data collected through passiona.ai. Passiona is an AI-literacy programme for schools in Hong Kong.
We design the public site to minimise personal-data collection. It has no visitor accounts, student profiles or behavioural advertising.

sections.heading: Enquiries and purpose of collection
paragraphs: When an adult submits an enquiry, we collect the name, school or organisation, and chosen enquiry type supplied in the form. Email address, WhatsApp number and enquiry details are optional.

We use these details only to respond to the requested free introductory lesson, demo, programme, partnership or funding enquiry, maintain an accurate record of that conversation, and arrange requested follow-up. Supplying the required fields is necessary for us to respond; optional fields are not required.
bullets: Please do not submit children’s personal data, sensitive information or unnecessary personal details in the enquiry form.
We do not use enquiry details for direct marketing unless we first obtain the consent required by applicable law.

sections.heading: Children and learning tools
paragraphs: The public website does not ask children to create accounts or provide names, contact details or other personal identifiers.

Where a learning activity uses live camera or microphone input, that input is intended to be processed on the device in memory for the activity. It is not used to create a child profile or retained by passiona.ai.

sections.heading: Cookies, logs and embedded media
paragraphs: We set the essential NEXT_LOCALE cookie to remember the language you choose. It expires after one year, is limited to this site, and does not contain your name or contact details.

Our hosting provider may process technical request information such as IP address, browser, device and server log data to deliver, secure and diagnose the site. Product demonstration videos load from YouTube only after you press Play; YouTube may then process data under its own policies.

sections.heading: Service providers and sharing
paragraphs: Passiona uses Cloudflare to host and deliver the website. If a lead-forwarding destination is configured, the adult enquiry details are sent securely to that service only so our team can respond. We require service providers to handle data for these purposes and with appropriate safeguards.
We do not sell personal data or disclose it for unrelated advertising. We may disclose information where required by law, to protect rights or safety, or as part of a lawful business transfer.

sections.heading: Retention and security
paragraphs: We keep enquiry data only for as long as needed to respond, manage the relationship, meet legal obligations or resolve a dispute. We then delete or anonymise it where practicable.
We use reasonable technical and organisational safeguards appropriate to the data and service, but no internet transmission or storage system can be guaranteed completely secure.

sections.heading: Your choices and requests
paragraphs: You may ask whether we hold your personal data and request access or correction. You may also ask us to delete enquiry data where applicable. Send the request through the site enquiry form and include enough information for us to identify the relevant record.

We handle requests in accordance with applicable law, including the Hong Kong Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance. This policy may change when our practices or the service changes; the date above shows the latest version.

sections.heading: About these terms
paragraphs: These terms govern use of passiona.ai and the Passiona materials made available through it. By using the site, you agree to them on your own behalf or, if you act for a school or organisation, on its behalf.

sections.heading: Educational use and supervision
paragraphs: Passiona is designed to support AI literacy. It is not a substitute for teacher judgement, safeguarding procedures, professional advice or independent assessment of an AI output.

Schools and educators are responsible for appropriate supervision, permissions, accessibility support and classroom use. Do not ask children to submit personal or sensitive information through the public site.
bullets: Use the site lawfully and do not interfere with its security, availability or operation.
Do not copy, reverse engineer, scrape, distribute or commercially exploit site materials except where law permits or Passiona agrees in writing.
Do not submit unlawful, harmful, infringing, deceptive or privacy-invasive material through the enquiry form.

sections.heading: AI, content and third parties
paragraphs: AI-related examples and learning materials are illustrative and may be incomplete, inaccurate or unsuitable for a particular context. Users should test, question and independently evaluate outputs.

The site may link to or embed third-party services, including YouTube. Those services are governed by their own terms and privacy policies; Passiona is not responsible for their content or availability.

sections.heading: Intellectual property
paragraphs: Passiona and its site content, designs, text, software, branding, images and media are protected by applicable intellectual-property laws. All rights not expressly granted are reserved.
You retain rights in information you submit, and grant Passiona a limited right to use it only to answer and administer your enquiry.

sections.heading: Availability, liability and changes
paragraphs: We may change, suspend or remove site content or functionality at any time. The site is provided on an ‘as is’ and ‘as available’ basis to the extent permitted by law.

To the extent permitted by law, Passiona excludes warranties and is not liable for indirect, incidental, special or consequential loss arising from use of the site. Nothing excludes liability that cannot lawfully be excluded.
We may update these terms by posting a new version. Continued use after the effective date means you accept the updated terms.

sections.heading: Governing law
paragraphs: These terms are governed by the laws of Hong Kong. The courts of Hong Kong have exclusive jurisdiction, except where applicable law requires otherwise. Questions about these terms may be sent through the site enquiry form.

Journey.title: A year-long journey from curiosity to confident judgement.
Journey.intro: Passiona gives each child a world they can keep building. The detail belongs in the classroom; the promise is simple: students learn to make, inspect and question AI.

stages.title: Build Your World
stages.body: Set up the city, Champion and Workshop before any AI concept.

stages.title: What AI Is, and How It Senses
stages.body: Rules, perception, outputs and the agent children direct.

stages.title: Learning from Data
stages.body: Models, evidence, uncertainty, numbers and unlabeled groups.

stages.title: Error, Agents & Systems
stages.body: Error costs, ensembles, bounded agents, environments and drift.

stages.title: Search, Design & Showcase
stages.body: Optimisation, real users and a proof-based final presentation.

Outcomes.intro: At the end of the programme, students can show not only what they made, but how they tested and judged it.

items.title: Trace a system
items.body: Explain what each part carries from input to output.

items.title: Test a claim fairly
items.body: Use new cases and evidence to check what an AI claim really shows.

items.title: Judge uncertainty
items.body: Consider error costs and when a human should decide.

items.title: Design for a real user

items.title: Present with proof
items.body: Explain a project clearly, show evidence and name one limitation.

Agent.title: AI agents, with children in charge.
Agent.intro: The programme makes an agent’s boundaries visible: a goal, permitted tools, a proposal, human approval and a checked result.
Agent.genericAlt: A tactile miniature diorama showing an AI agent inside a visible task boundary with a human approval gate
Agent.previewDescription: A static Coding Buddy chat preview. A child explains that the school gate is busy after lessons and asks to make crossing safer. The Buddy may use the city map and traffic data, proposes a safe crossing while keeping the bus stop clear, and asks the child to approve or change it. The result is verified against the city plan.
Agent.previewChildMessage: The school gate gets busy after lessons. Can we make crossing safer?
Agent.previewBuddyMessage: I found a busy crossing near the school gate. I can plan a safer route with the map and traffic data.
Agent.previewProposal: Add a safe crossing by the school and keep the bus stop clear.
Agent.previewDecisionQuestion: Would you like to add this?
Agent.genericTitle: Goal → tools → proposal → approval → checked result
Agent.genericBody: A model can generate an answer. An agent also chooses an action in an environment. Children learn to ask what the agent is allowed to touch, what it proposed and how they can check or undo the result.

ProgrammePrinciples.label: How Passiona builds judgement and trust
ProgrammePrinciples.progressionIntro: The year moves from making a system work to composing systems for a user—and defending the result with evidence.

progression.title: Builder
progression.body: Make a system run and trace its parts.

progression.title: Skeptic
progression.body: Test the claim on cases the machine has not seen.

progression.title: Auditor
progression.body: Find error costs, uncertainty, drift and honest limits.

progression.title: Architect
progression.body: Compose tools for a real user and defend the evidence.

ProgrammePrinciples.evidenceTitle: Evidence is part of every lesson
ProgrammePrinciples.evidenceIntro: Children practise held-out testing, correct, wrong and unsure outcomes, explainability, thresholds, error costs, approval logs and honest limitations long before the showcase.

evidence.title: Held-out testing
evidence.body: Training examples are not proof. New cases show whether a model has learned or memorised.

evidence.title: Correct, wrong and not sure
evidence.body: Students compare outcomes instead of treating every confident label as truth.

evidence.title: Explainability
evidence.body: Nearest examples, routes, receipts and visible mappings make decisions inspectable.

evidence.title: Thresholds and error costs
evidence.body: A safer system may abstain; children decide what a false alarm or missed case costs.

evidence.title: Approval logs and limitations
evidence.body: A project is not finished until its authorised changes and one honest limitation are named.

ProgrammePrinciples.trustTitle: Children stay in control of the work.
ProgrammePrinciples.trustIntro: Clear boundaries, visible evidence and privacy-minded tools help schools teach AI with confidence.

privacy.title: Camera and microphone stay in memory
privacy.body: Live input is processed on the device for the activity and is not kept as a child profile.

privacy.title: No child PII
privacy.body: The programme does not require child names, accounts or personal identifiers to learn.

privacy.title: Students control saving
privacy.body: Work is saved by the student through a Champion File; restore is one tap, and cloud codes contain no account or PII.
